metadata.title: Learning Local Image Descriptors with Deep Siamese and Triplet Convolutional Networks by Minimizing Global Loss Functions

nodes.name: Mahalanobis Distance
nodes.statement: The squared Mahalanobis distance between points x_i and x_j is defined as d_W = (x_i - x_j)^T W (x_i - x_j), where W is a positive semi-definite matrix parameterising the metric.

nodes.name: Deep ConvNet Definition
nodes.statement: A deep ConvNet is defined as f(x, theta_f) = f_out composed with r_L composed with h_L composed with f_L ... composed with r_1 composed with h_1 composed with f_1(x), where f_l is the pre-activation function (linear transforms in convolutional layers), h_l is a normalisation function, and r_l is a non-linear activation function such as ReLU.

nodes.name: Siamese Network
nodes.statement: A siamese network consists of two identical deep ConvNets with tied weights, trained using pairs of labelled inputs. It can produce either a feature embedding or a pairwise similarity estimation depending on architecture and loss function.

nodes.name: Triplet Network
nodes.statement: The triplet network is an extension of the siamese network that is trained with triplets at the input (x, x^+, x^-), where x and x^+ belong to the same class and x^- belongs to a different class. It produces a feature embedding using three identical (weight-tied) ConvNet towers.

nodes.name: Siamese Pairwise Embedding Loss (J_1^s)
nodes.statement: The pairwise loss for a siamese network producing an embedding is J_1^s(x_i, x_j, theta_f) = delta(y_i - y_j) ||f(x_i) - f(x_j)||_2 - (1 - delta(y_i - y_j)) ||f(x_i) - f(x_j)||_2, which minimises distance between same-class pairs and maximises distance between different-class pairs.

nodes.name: Siamese Pairwise Similarity Loss (J_2^s)
nodes.statement: The pairwise similarity loss for a siamese network is J_2^s(x_i, x_j, theta_g) = delta(y_i - y_j)(1/(kappa + g(x_i, x_j, theta_g))) + (1 - delta(y_i - y_j)) g(x_i, x_j, theta_g), where g returns a similarity score and kappa is a small positive constant.

nodes.name: Triplet Loss (J_1^t)
nodes.statement: The triplet loss is J_1^t(x, x^+, x^-, theta_f) = max(0, 1 - ||f(x) - f(x^-)||_2 / (||f(x) - f(x^+)||_2 + m)), where m is a margin, x^+ is same-class as x, and x^- is a different class. It provides relative context by jointly considering similar and dissimilar pairs in each triplet.

nodes.name: Global Loss for Feature Embedding (J_1^g)
nodes.statement: The proposed global loss for feature embedding is J_1^g = (sigma^{2+} + sigma^{2-}) + lambda * max(0, mu^+ - mu^- + t), where mu^+, sigma^{2+} are mean and variance of matching pair distances, mu^-, sigma^{2-} are mean and variance of non-matching pair distances, lambda balances the terms, and t is the margin. Distances are d_i^+ = ||f(x_i) - f(x_i^+)||_2^2 / 4 and d_i^- = ||f(x_i) - f(x_i^-)||_2^2 / 4, constrained to [0,1].

nodes.name: Gradient of Global Embedding Loss
nodes.statement: The gradient of J_1^g with respect to f(x_i) depends on global statistics mu^+ and mu^- of the training set (not just the i-th triplet), which suppresses spurious gradients from outliers and improves generalisation compared to the triplet loss gradient which depends only on the i-th triplet.

nodes.name: Global Loss for Pairwise Similarity (J_2^g)
nodes.statement: The global loss for pairwise similarity estimation is J_2^g = (sigma^{2+} + sigma^{2-}) + lambda * max(0, m - (mu^+ - mu^-)), where mu^+ and sigma^{2+} are mean and variance of matching pair similarities, mu^- and sigma^{2-} are mean and variance of non-matching pair similarities. It minimises variance of both distributions, minimises mean non-matching similarity, and maximises mean matching similarity.

nodes.name: Gradient of Global Pairwise Similarity Loss
nodes.statement: The gradient of J_2^g with respect to g(x_i, x_i^+) is (2/N)[(g(x_i, x_i^+) - mu^+) - (1/2) * indicator((mu^+ - mu^-) < m)], and similarly for non-matching pairs with reversed sign on the indicator term.

nodes.name: Combined Triplet and Global Loss (J_1^{tg})
nodes.statement: The combined loss is J_1^{tg} = gamma * sum_j J_1^t(x_j, x_j^+, x_j^-) + J_1^g({x_i}, {x_i^+}, {x_i^-}), combining the per-triplet triplet loss with the global embedding loss weighted by gamma.

nodes.name: Model 1: TNet, TLoss
nodes.statement: The first proposed model is a triplet network trained with the triplet loss J_1^t, which produces a feature embedding. Architecture: B(96,7,3)-P(2,2)-B(192,5,1)-P(2,2)-B(256,3,1)-B(256,1,1)-B(256,1,1), where B(n,k,s) is a block with convolution C(n,k,s) followed by batch normalisation and ReLU.

nodes.name: Model 2: TNet, TGLoss
nodes.statement: The second proposed model is a triplet network producing an embedding, trained with the combined triplet and global loss J_1^{tg}. It uses the same architecture as TNet-TLoss and is initialised from TNet-TLoss weights trained for 50 epochs, then trained for 50 more epochs with the combined loss.

nodes.name: Model 3: SNet, GLoss
nodes.statement: The third proposed model is a siamese network producing a pairwise similarity estimation, trained with the global pairwise similarity loss J_2^g. Architecture: B(96,7,3)-P(2,2)-B(192,5,1)-P(2,2)-B(256,3,1)-B(256,1,1)-C(1,1,1).

nodes.name: Model 4: CS SNet, GLoss
nodes.statement: The fourth proposed model is the central-surround siamese network producing pairwise similarity, trained with the global loss J_2^g. It uses a multi-resolution central-surround architecture: B(95,5,1)-P(2,2)-B(96,3,1)-P(2,2)-B(192,3,1)-B(192,3,1) for each stream, combined by B(768,2,1)-C(1,1,1).

nodes.name: Triplet Network Improves Over Siamese for Descriptor Learning
nodes.statement: The triplet network (TNet-TLoss) produces a more accurate embedding than the siamese network for local image descriptor learning on the UBC benchmark dataset.
assumptions: Training and testing on the UBC benchmark dataset with six combinations of Liberty, Notredame, and Yosemite sets
Feature embedding comparison using L2 norm distance
conclusions: TNet-TLoss achieves mean FPR95 of 9.63%, improving over Siam-l2 (13.45%) on the UBC dataset

nodes.name: Combined Triplet+Global Loss Produces Best Embedding
nodes.statement: The combination of the triplet and global losses (TNet-TGLoss) produces the best feature embedding result in the field on the UBC dataset, with mean FPR95 of 8.8%.
assumptions: Training and testing on UBC benchmark dataset
TNet-TGLoss initialised from TNet-TLoss trained for 50 epochs then trained for 50 more epochs with combined loss
Hyperparameters gamma=1, t=0.4, lambda=0.8 estimated via cross validation
conclusions: TNet-TGLoss achieves mean FPR95 of 8.8%, the best embedding result on the UBC dataset, improving over TNet-TLoss (9.63%) and siam-2stream-l2 (9.67%)
TNet-TGLoss embedding outperforms even some pairwise similarity methods (Siam and 512d-F(512))

nodes.name: CS SNet with Global Loss Produces Best Pairwise Similarity Result
nodes.statement: The central-surround siamese network trained with the global loss (CS SNet, GLoss) produces the best classification result on the UBC dataset in the pairwise similarity category, nearly halving the previous state-of-the-art FPR95.
assumptions: Training and testing on UBC benchmark dataset
Randomly initialised weights trained for 80 epochs
Hyperparameters m=1, lambda=1 estimated via cross validation
conclusions: CS SNet GLoss achieves mean FPR95 of 2.71%, nearly halving the previous state-of-the-art (2ch-2stream at 4.19%)
CS SNet GLoss achieves the best result on all six train/test combinations

nodes.name: Global Loss is Robust to Outliers
nodes.statement: The global loss function is more robust to outliers than the standard triplet loss, as demonstrated on a 2D toy dataset with 5% label noise. The global loss gradient depends on training set statistics (mu^+, mu^-), which suppresses spurious gradients from outliers.
assumptions: 2D toy dataset with 80 samples from two Gaussian distributions
5% label noise (4 samples with switched labels)
ConvNet mapping to 128-dimensional embedding with structure B(256,2,1)-B(512,1,1)-C(128,1,1)
Evaluation by nearest-neighbour classification in embedding space
conclusions: Triplet loss alone overfits to outliers, producing incorrect labelling at outlier locations
Combined triplet and global losses reduce labelling mistakes caused by outliers
Global loss alone produces coherent label maps even at outlier locations

nodes.name: Pairwise Similarity Methods Outperform Embedding Methods
nodes.statement: Siamese networks trained with pairwise similarity loss achieve better classification performance than feature embeddings produced by triplet loss, but at the cost of higher inference complexity since pairwise similarity requires a forward pass through the network for each comparison.
assumptions: Embedding comparison uses cosine distance (simplified L2 due to unit norm)
Pairwise similarity requires the final fully connected layer for each pair
conclusions: Pairwise similarity methods (e.g., CS SNet GLoss at 2.71%) outperform embedding methods (e.g., TNet-TGLoss at 8.8%)
However, TNet-TGLoss embedding (8.8%) outperforms some pairwise similarity methods like Siam (10.07%) and 512d-F(512) (9.82%)
